title: DNA Replication in Eukaryotic Cells — Priming, Leading and Lagging Strand Synthesis

events.caption: One fork, two antiparallel templates
events.action: Start with an already-open blue Y-shaped fork linked to a short parental duplex on the right. Establish upper/lower template end polarities; keep it throughout.

events.caption: Primase makes an RNA starting point
events.action: Purple primase contacts a site; orange RNA primer appears nucleotide by nucleotide. Mark exposed 3prime end. A primed 5prime end does not grow.

events.caption: DNA polymerase extends 5prime to 3prime
events.action: Cyan polymerase remains at the growing end; separate green nucleotide Mobjects accumulate along the upper blue template toward fork. Keep correct 5prime and 3prime labels.

events.caption: Continuous leading; short lagging fragments
events.action: At the same fork, leading synthesis continues. Lower template gets at least two orange primers nearer advancing fork; each green fragment extends left from its own RNA 3prime end, away from fork. Use stable identities and attached active-site anchors.

events.caption: Remove RNA, fill DNA, then seal a nick
events.action: First fade/remove a lower orange primer; show gap. Polymerase adds green DNA into gap, leaving a nick; only then gold ligase contacts nick and seals without adding DNA. End with local copied duplexes.

continuity: One stable fork and stable blue templates persist; concise changing English caption, no left lecture panel; at most 1–2 main callouts at once.
